Construct values

Decimals, integers, and fractions

Use a string literal for a decimal constant, the constructor for text read at runtime, and a rational for an exact fraction. The result is represented as a DoubleFloat in each case.

using DoubleFloats

from_literal = df64"0.2"
from_text = Double64("0.2")
from_fraction = Double64(1 // 5)
from_float = Double64(0.2)

@assert from_literal == from_text == from_fraction
@assert from_float != from_literal
nothing

Julia rounds an ordinary decimal literal to Float64 before calling the constructor. Widening is appropriate for data that already consists of Float64 values. For smaller types, use df32"…" or df16"…".

Small integers such as Double64(2) convert exactly. The integer constructor converts through the underlying float, so large integers can round before the low component is formed. Use a rational or a decimal string when the integer has more bits than the underlying float can hold.

Create a complex number from two values of the same precision, for example ComplexDF64(df64"0.2", df64"0.3"). Julia's exact constants also work directly, for example Double64(pi).

Working with two components

Use DoubleFloat(hi, lo) to represent the sum of two floats of the same type in normalized form. HILO(x) retrieves the stored pair. The two-component constructor Double64(hi, lo) with two Float64 arguments stores the components as supplied. It is useful when restoring an existing pair whose components are already normalized.

using DoubleFloats

x = DoubleFloat(1.0, 2.0^-60)
hi, lo = HILO(x)
@assert Double64(hi, lo) === x
nothing

See Display and parse values to work with decimal text, and Representation and precision for the meaning of the two components.
